sources.section: Communication - Email - Mailing Lists and Newsletters
sources.entry: Keila - Reliable and easy-to-use newsletter tool (alternative to Mailchimp and Sendinblue). (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Keila is an open source newsletter tool for sending email campaigns and creating sign-up forms, positioned as an alternative to Mailchimp and Sendinblue.
summary.what_it_does: Keila lets you send newsletter campaigns and build sign-up forms. For smaller newsletters, it can send campaigns through your own email inbox via SMTP. For larger projects, the README says it supports AWS SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, and Postmark in addition to SMTP. The README offers a hosted version at app.keila.io with paid pricing for Keila Cloud, and a self-hosted option using the official Docker image pentacent/keila or a sample Docker Compose config in the repo. Installation details are in separate docs that the README links to but does not reproduce. Contributions of code and translations are welcomed, per CONTRIBUTING.md.
use_cases: send newsletters through AWS SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, or Postmark
how_to_run: Use the sample Docker Compose config in the repository
Follow the Installation Docs linked from the README
notable: Supports multiple transactional email providers in addition to plain SMTP
Can use a personal email inbox for small newsletters
Official Docker image and sample Docker Compose config
caveats: Keila Cloud, the hosted version, has paid pricing
Self-hosting installation is described in separate docs, not in the README itself
Larger newsletter setups rely on external email providers such as SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, or Postmark
keywords: send newsletter from my own inbox
